manifest_findings.title: Service (in.veris.app.VerisCallScreeningService) is Protected by a permission, but the protection level of the permission should be checked. Permission: android.permission.BIND_SCREENING_SERVICE [android:exported=true]
manifest_findings.description: A Service is found to be shared with other apps on the device therefore leaving it accessible to any other application on the device. It is protected by a permission which is not defined in the analysed application. As a result, the protection level of the permission should be checked where it is defined. If it is set to normal or dangerous, a malicious application can request and obtain the permission and interact with the component. If it is set to signature, only applications signed with the same certificate can obtain the permission.
manifest_findings.name: Service in.veris.app.VerisCallScreeningService is Protected by a permission, but the protection level of the permission should be checked. [Permission: android.permission.BIND_SCREENING_SERVICE] [android:exported=true]

manifest_findings.title: Activity (in.veris.app.MainActivity) is vulnerable to Android Task Hijacking/StrandHogg.
manifest_findings.description: An Activity should not be having the launch mode attribute set to "singleTask". It is then possible for other applications to place a malicious activity on top of the activity stack resulting in Task Hijacking/StrandHogg 1.0 vulnerability. This makes the application an easy target for phishing attacks. The vulnerability can be remediated by setting the launch mode attribute to "singleInstance" or by setting an empty taskAffinity (taskAffinity="") attribute. You can also update the target SDK version (24) of the app to 28 or higher to fix this issue at platform level.
manifest_findings.name: Activity (in.veris.app.MainActivity) is vulnerable to Android Task Hijacking/StrandHogg.

manifest_findings.title: Activity (in.veris.app.MainActivity) is vulnerable to StrandHogg 2.0
manifest_findings.description: Activity is found to be vulnerable to StrandHogg 2.0 task hijacking vulnerability. When vulnerable, it is possible for other applications to place a malicious activity on top of the activity stack of the vulnerable application. This makes the application an easy target for phishing attacks. The vulnerability can be remediated by setting the launch mode attribute to "singleInstance" and by setting an empty taskAffinity (taskAffinity=""). You can also update the target SDK version (24) of the app to 29 or higher to fix this issue at platform level.
manifest_findings.name: Activity (in.veris.app.MainActivity) is vulnerable to StrandHogg 2.0

manifest_findings.title: TaskAffinity is set for activity (expo.modules.webbrowser.BrowserProxyActivity)
manifest_findings.description: If taskAffinity is set, then other application could read the Intents sent to Activities belonging to another task. Always use the default setting keeping the affinity as the package name in order to prevent sensitive information inside sent or received Intents from being read by another application.
manifest_findings.name: TaskAffinity is set for Activity (expo.modules.webbrowser.BrowserProxyActivity)

high.title: Activity (in.veris.app.MainActivity) is vulnerable to Android Task Hijacking/StrandHogg.
high.description: An Activity should not be having the launch mode attribute set to "singleTask". It is then possible for other applications to place a malicious activity on top of the activity stack resulting in Task Hijacking/StrandHogg 1.0 vulnerability. This makes the application an easy target for phishing attacks. The vulnerability can be remediated by setting the launch mode attribute to "singleInstance" or by setting an empty taskAffinity (taskAffinity="") attribute. You can also update the target SDK version (24) of the app to 28 or higher to fix this issue at platform level.
